focus.jbig: Oil below $100 · Oracle beat lifts futures · but CPI at 8:30 ET, FOMC next week
focus.jtag: Crude retreats below $100 as Hormuz flows hold up and Oracle's results boost tech; futures bounce after a four-day slide, but August CPI is the print that decides the Fed
focus.jnote: The tape catches a relief bid into the day’s big data point. WTI crude slid back below $100 to ~$99.42 after the U.S. Energy Secretary said more than 17 million barrels moved through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday — easing supply fears — and the IEA cut its 2026 demand forecast; Brent pulled back from ~$105 toward ~$103. Oracle’s better-than-expected results boosted tech sentiment, and S&P futures are up ~0.5% with Nasdaq contracts ~0.6% higher after four straight down days. But the 10-year yield is still near a three-year high (~4.95%) and the whole session hinges on August CPI at 8:30 ET — the last inflation read before the FOMC on 9/15–16. A relief bounce into a CPI print that can reprice the Fed is not a premium-selling setup.
focus.notdown: Energy (XLE, XOM, MPC, OXY) and Defense (LMT, RTX, NOC) keep a structural war-premium bid, but today they’re actually the fade group as crude gives back the spike — a reminder these are two-sided war trades, not clean Snipers. One Hormuz-easing headline (like this morning’s) gaps energy straight back down. Watch-only, and note the one boarded name (ZIM) is flagged thinly traded.
focus.notup: Rate-sensitive growth and fuel-sensitive transports (airlines) get temporary relief from lower oil, but a hot CPI at 8:30 ET can reprice the curve and slam both. Selling bear calls into a data-day bounce, with an FOMC hike debate next week that can break either way, is exactly the blow-up 4-VAL exists to prevent. The disciplined answer is to sell nothing new today.
focus.why: Why RED? Composite 58 is squarely WARM and P(≥1% gap) at 44% is above the 35% trigger — either one alone locks out GREEN. More important: August CPI hits at 8:30 ET today and the FOMC (9/15–16) lands inside a normal DTE, and with crude having just topped $100 the oil pass-through makes an upside surprise more likely than usual. The one boarded name (ZIM) is flagged illiquid / OI-thin / liquidity-unverified. Stand down on new credit spreads, or if you must be positioned, use 7-DTE that clears CPI and the FOMC and cut size hard. Cash is a position today.

risks: August CPI · today 8:30 ET — the last inflation print before the FOMC; consensus ~0.4% m/m and ~3.4% y/y headline. With crude having just topped $100 the oil pass-through makes an upside surprise more likely than usual — a hot number hardens hike odds and can erase the pre-market bounce. The single biggest event of the day.

FOMC · Mon–Wed 9/15–16 — a live hike-or-hold meeting; markets price ~50–58% odds of a 25bp move after a strong August jobs report and hawkish commentary from Chair Warsh. Any spread must expire before this.

Oil & the 10-year — WTI eased below $100 and Brent near $103 today, but the 10Y is near a three-year high (~4.95%). Any renewed oil pop or a yield break higher compounds pressure on stocks and hardens the hike case.

Iran / Strait of Hormuz — today’s relief came from confirmation that ~17M+ barrels flowed through Hormuz Monday, but the conflict is live. Any strike on shipping reverses the oil-easing move instantly — the week’s biggest tail.

Thin single-name liquidity — the one boarded name (ZIM) is flagged OI-thin (37) and one-sided; its scanner price is also stale vs the ~$30.37 pre-market. Confirm a real ATM market before ever attempting a fill.
